newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court classifies echinacea products as medications not foods.
newsitem.headline: Court classifies echinacea products as medications not foods.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday extracts of echinacea in alcohol designed to combat colds and flu should be classified for customs tax purposes as medications.

After a challenge between Bioforce and German tax authorities, a federal court in Germany asked the court to decide whether products such as Echinacea drops and Echinaforce should be classified as medication, spirituous beverages designed to maintain well-being, or food supplements.
The court chose Common Customs Tariff classification heading 3004, because the objective characteristics and properties of echinacea products are most closely linked with medications.

The court said "whatever the actual therapeutic or prophylactic value of the products in question, it must be held that the curative properties of the products as well as the way they are packaged, dispensed and marketed are in themselves such as to cause them to be regarded as products possessing the characteristics properties of a medicament."
Reference from the Finanzgericht Munchen (Germany) for a preliminary ruling between

on the interpretation of headings 3004 and 2208 of Annex I to Commission regulation (EEC) No 2551/93 of 10 August 1993 Annex I to Council regulation (EEC) No 2658/87 on the tariff and statistical nomenclature and on the Common Customs Tariff (OJ 1993 L 241, p. 1), on the classification of enchinacea drops

The Common Customs Tariff, in the version established in Annex I to Commission regulation (EEC) No 2551/93 of 10 August 1993 Annex I to Council regulation (EEC) No 2658/87 on the tariff and statistical nomenclature and on the Common Customs Tariff must be interpreted as meaning that Echinacea purpurea extract-based drops must be classified under heading 3004.
